description:
The transit staging WAL (crates/transit/src/staging.rs) already implements the correct durability contract: article written to disk + SQLite row committed before 239 is sent to the peer. On restart, unprocessed staging rows are replayed automatically.

However [staging] is optional config. When absent, the daemon uses the in-memory ingestion queue and sends 239 before anything is durable. If the process dies after 239 but before block_put, the peer thinks we have the article, we don't, and nobody knows. The peer will not re-offer it (we already ACKed). Article is silently lost.

## Fix

Add a config validation rule matching the signing key pattern:

  if listen.addr binds a non-loopback address AND staging is None:
      return Err(ConfigError::Validation(
          "[staging] must be configured when listening on a non-loopback address.            The staging WAL ensures 239/235 is only sent after the article is durably            written to disk. Run with a loopback address for dev mode without staging."
      ))

Loopback-only deployments (dev, test) can continue without staging.

## Also fix

The ec2_s3_runbook.md does not mention [staging] config at all. Add a staging section to the runbook showing the required config:

  [staging]
  path = "/srv/stoa/transit/staging"
  max_bytes = 5368709120   # 5 GiB
  max_entries = 500000

## Note on the reader

The reader comment in staging.rs notes: 'When an article is staged but has not yet been written to IPFS, any reader request for that Message-ID must be served directly from the staging file. That integration point lives in the reader server ARTICLE/HEAD/BODY handler and is wired in when those handlers are implemented.' This is a separate gap — reader may return 430 No Such Article for an article that is staged but not yet in the block store. File a separate issue for that.
title: fix: require staging WAL for non-loopback transit deployments
